newsitem.title: CANADA: British Columbia lumber labor talks set for May.
newsitem.headline: British Columbia lumber labor talks set for May.

text.p: Labor negotiations for British Columbia's coastal lumber industry will begin May 5, the IWA-Canada union and employers' bargaining agent Forest Industrial Relations said Monday.

The current contract covering about 14,000 coastal lumber workers expires June 15. Another contract covering about 13,000 lumber workers in the interior of British Columbia expires June 30. The interior contract is usually patterned after the coastal agreement.

IWA-Canada spokesman Norm Garcia said the union's main demands will be for a "substantial" wage increase, a shorter work week with no loss in pay, job security and assurances on contracting out of work.
MacMillan Bloedel Ltd and Pacific Forest Products Ltd intend to bargain with the union separately.
But Forest Industrial Relations executive Keith Bennett said MacMillan Bloedel may return to the joint talks depending on the outcome of a Labor Relations Board action now underway.
In that proceeding, the union is seeking to certify all MacMillan Bloedel locations to bargain together.

Bennett said that he anticipated that this round of contract talks would follow the past pattern and be difficult. Some of the union's demands, such as the wage increase and shorter work week, would likely be problemmatic, he said. ((Reuters Vancouver Bureau (604) 664-7314))
